To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chemokine and cytokines synergize to promote eosinophil migration in allergic inflammation.
eosinophils are recruited into the asthmatic airway by a unique chemokine, eotaxin, in concert with the eosinophil chemoattractant, IL‐5.
eosinophil migration is a multistep process regulated by a complex network of chemokines and chemokine‐like cytokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate eosionophil migration in asthma.
the role of chemokines and chemokine receptors in eosinophil migration in asthma.
the role of chemokines and their receptors in the pathophysiological processes that lead to allergic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

eosinophil chemotaxis in the asthmatics response is a complex phenomenon involving the cooperation of multiple chemokines and/or cytokines, which are capable of interacting with each other in a synergistic manner.
chemokine/cyokine cooperativity plays an important role in eosinophil migration in allergic disease.
the mechanisms of chemokine and cytokines cooperativity are complex and are not fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the eosinophil is the central cell type in asthma and that it has a number of unique properties which allow it to migrate into tissues in response to chemokine/cyokine cooperativity.

the mechanisms whereby eosnophils migrate are complex; however there exists a unique synergistic relationship between eotaxins and IL-5 that appears to play an important role in eosinophil migration in vivo.
chemokines and IL‐5 are important for the migration of eosinophils into the airway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokines and their receptors play a critical role in the regulation of eosinophil migration and that chemokine/cyteokine cooperativity is an important feature in the regulation of allergic disease.
the eosinophil response to eotaxin requires the presence of other cytokines.
chemokines and their receptors are not just passive markers of disease, but are key players in disease pathogenesis.
